result.summary:
Independently re-gated docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-029.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ-029, commit d418bc5) against WF-02 Step 3b's three checks, without trusting TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary as a substitute for reading the artefact and the real code.

Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3b, docs/agents/design/REQ-029.md in full (all 7 ACs), and docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-029.md in full.

1) Verified the xmin claim (AC2's zero-write proof). `apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts`: grepped every `updatedAt`/`updated_at` occurrence (10 hits) and confirmed none carries `.$onUpdate()` anywhere in the file -- registrations' own updatedAt (line 278) is a plain `timestamp(...).notNull().defaultNow()` with no update hook. `grep -rn TRIGGER apps/bot/drizzle/*.sql` returned zero matches across all 6 migration files (0000-0005) -- no Postgres BEFORE/AFTER UPDATE trigger exists anywhere that could touch `registrations.updated_at` (or any column) as a side effect. This confirms updated_at genuinely cannot serve as a 'did an UPDATE run' proxy in this schema, and Postgres's own hidden xmin system column (a new MVCC tuple version id is created by every UPDATE regardless of which columns its SET clause names) is a valid, structurally necessary substitute -- not an overcomplicated solution when a simpler proxy exists, since no simpler proxy exists here.

2) Rigorously traced the stale-token sub-case B reasoning against the actual committed handler, `apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.ts`'s `resolveCheckinQrDeepLink` (lines 55-139). Line 64: `const lookup = await getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin(db, qrToken, lang)` -- this is the unlocked, by-current-qr_token-value lookup. Lines 65-68: `if (lookup === null) { await ctx.reply(catalog.checkinQr.unknownToken); return; }` -- an immediate, unconditional return BEFORE `performQrCheckIn` is called at all (that call sits at line 97, only reached if the function did not already return at line 68). Since `getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin` queries by `qr_token = $qrToken` (design section 2.1), a superseded token T1 (one a live row no longer carries, because registerForEvent issued a new T2 onto the same registrationId per REQ-022's row-reuse behavior) matches zero rows and this lookup returns null -- so under ordinary, sequential /start dispatch, scanning T1 refuses at line 66 and `performQrCheckIn`'s own internal step-2 token-currency recheck (registration.ts, the `row.qrToken !== qrToken` check inside the locked transaction) is never reached. TEST-DESIGNER's trace is CORRECT: only a direct call to `performQrCheckIn(db, R, T1, ...)` (bypassing the earlier unlocked lookup entirely, as sub-case B does) or a genuine race (an unlocked read racing a concurrent re-registration's commit) can exercise that specific line. Sub-case B is therefore a legitimate, non-redundant test, not a duplicate of sub-case A -- confirmed by direct code reading, not by taking the spec's own claim on trust.

3) Verified AC1/AC3/AC5/AC6 against the real schema/decision tables, not just the design doc's prose: `apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts`'s `eventStaff` table (line 302) carries `uq_event_staff_event_user` unique on `(eventId, userId)` -- confirming AC1's cross-event-staff fixture (staff for Event Y only, scanning Event X's token) is a genuine test of eventId-scoped membership, not reducible to BACKEND-DEV's 'never staff anywhere' fixture. `apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts`'s actual `decideQrCheckinOutcome` (lines 1229-1240) and `decideOverrideOutcome` (lines 1342-1350) match the spec's stated first-match-wins tables exactly -- confirming AC3's three-state cycle (waitlisted/requested/withdrawn, each its own outcome.admission carried through to the catalog-key table in checkinQr.ts's REFUSAL_CATALOG_KEY, lines 30-36) and AC6's positive/negative split are exercising the real code, not an imagined one. `companyPlaceholder` (checkinQr.ts lines 41-43: `company !== null ? \` — ${company}\` : \"\"`) confirms AC5's null-company sub-case's 'no orphan  —  separator' assertion is checking the actual branch. `requireOrganizerForChapter` (eventAuthorization.ts lines 81-88) delegates to `checkOrganizerForChapter(user, targetChapterId)`, confirming AC6's negative case (an organizer scoped to a DIFFERENT chapter) genuinely exercises chapter-scoping rather than a role-presence check BACKEND-DEV's plain-EventStaff negative case cannot reach.

4) Verified no mocked/stubbed grammY Context anywhere: grepped the spec for mock/jest.fn/vi.fn/'as unknown as Context'/stub -- zero matches. Every case (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6 positive/negative, stale-token sub-case A) dispatches through real `bot.handleUpdate()`/`commandUpdate`/`callbackUpdate` per the Shared Setup section's `makeTestBot()` helper, modeled on BACKEND-DEV's own already-committed checkinQr.db.test.ts pattern. Sub-case B is explicitly and correctly labeled 'direct call, the defensive code path itself' (not 'dispatch') and calls `performQrCheckIn` directly, a domain function that takes no Context argument at all -- there is no Context to mock in that sub-case, and the spec does not miscategorize it as a dispatch anywhere; its own dedicated section states plainly it supplements, not replaces, sub-case A's full-dispatch case.

5) Each case states its own failure mode explicitly and specifically (AC1: staff-membership check missing an eventId filter; AC2: an accidental no-op UPDATE writing back identical values; AC3: a REFUSAL_CATALOG_KEY swap or an admission-gated override-button regression; AC5: a query widened to include phone/email, or a companyPlaceholder regression rendering a bare separator; AC6: requireOrganizerForChapter checking 'organizer for any chapter' instead of 'for this event's chapter'; stale-token: performQrCheckIn dropping its qr_token recheck) -- none reduce to 'check it looks right.'

Gate checks: (a) every acceptance criterion has >=1 verification case -- AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5/AC6 each have a dedicated, precise case; AC4 is correctly deferred to BACKEND-DEV's already-committed checkinQr.db.test.ts with a stated reason (no gap found on direct read); AC7 is correctly handled as a git grep check, not a vitest case, per Step 3's own scope-test framing for non-behavioral verification -- PASS. (b) no TODO left -- grep -in TODO on the spec returned zero matches -- PASS. (c) each case is precise enough to run without judgment -- every case names the exact fixture (down to specific names/tokens/chapter counts), exact dispatch sequence (real command/callback update payloads), and exact pass/fail assertions (exact catalog keys, exact SQL predicates, exact xmin/audit-row counts) -- PASS.

No file-existence fabrication found: the spec correctly and repeatedly states apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.forgery.test.ts does not exist yet and will be written by TEST-RUNNER at Step 4, matching the REQ-026/027/028 precedent -- confirmed via `git log --all --oneline -- apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.forgery.test.ts` returning nothing.

No issues found requiring rework.

checks.every_ac_has_a_case: PASS -- AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5/AC6 each have a dedicated new case; AC4 correctly deferred to BACKEND-DEV's committed checkinQr.db.test.ts with a stated no-gap finding; AC7 correctly handled as a git grep check, not a vitest case; the stale-token S4 recheck (flagged reachable-but-untested by SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR) has a dedicated two-sub-case section.
checks.no_todo_left: PASS -- grep -in TODO on docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-029.md: zero matches.
checks.cases_precise_and_runnable: PASS -- every case names the exact fixture, exact dispatch/call sequence, and exact pass/fail assertions (exact catalog keys, exact SQL/xmin predicates, exact counts) -- none rely on a subjective 'looks right' judgment.
checks.xmin_claim_verified: PASS -- grep confirms registrations.updatedAt (schema.ts line 278) has no .$onUpdate(), and grep -rn TRIGGER over all 6 apps/bot/drizzle/*.sql migrations returns zero matches -- updated_at cannot serve as a zero-write proxy in this schema, making xmin a valid and necessary substitute, not an overcomplication.
checks.stale_token_subcase_b_trace_verified: PASS -- direct read of apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.ts's resolveCheckinQrDeepLink (lines 55-139) confirms the unlocked getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin lookup (line 64) returns null and unconditionally returns (line 66-68) BEFORE performQrCheckIn is ever called (line 97) when the token is superseded -- so under ordinary sequential dispatch, only a direct performQrCheckIn call (sub-case B) or a genuine race can reach performQrCheckIn's own internal token-currency recheck. TEST-DESIGNER's trace is accurate.
checks.ac_details_verified_against_real_code: PASS -- eventStaff's (eventId,userId) unique index confirms AC1's cross-event-staff distinction is genuine; decideQrCheckinOutcome/decideOverrideOutcome's actual implementations match the spec's stated tables for AC3; companyPlaceholder's actual null-check confirms AC5's null-company sub-case targets the real branch; requireOrganizerForChapter's actual chapter-scoped delegation confirms AC6's negative case targets the real authorization boundary.
checks.no_mocked_context: PASS -- zero mock/jest.fn/vi.fn/stub hits in the spec; every case dispatches through real bot.handleUpdate() except sub-case B, which is explicitly and correctly labeled a direct domain-function call (performQrCheckIn takes no Context at all), not miscategorized as a dispatch.
checks.failure_modes_stated: PASS -- every case states a specific, mechanism-level failure mode, not a vague description.
